# Jane Doe — 2024 Schedule C / SE Tax Workpaper
Single-member LLC, disregarded entity. Cash method. Single filer. No W-2 wages assumed.

## 1. Gross-Receipts Reconciliation

1099s double-count $18,000 paid by Bluefin *through* PayFlow. 1099-K is reported **gross**; bank received PayFlow **net** of 3%.

| Item | Amount ($) | Method / Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| 1099-NEC — Northwind Analytics Inc., ACH | 62,000 | Include in full — cash received, no withholding |
| 1099-NEC — Bluefin Health LLC | 56,500 | Include in full, but eliminate duplicate below |
| 1099-K — PayFlow Payments, gross | 40,700 | Include in full — comprises $18,000 Bluefin + $22,700 small clients |
| Less: duplicate — Bluefin via PayFlow in both NEC and K | (18,000) | Deduct once to avoid double-count |
| **Gross receipts, per information returns** | **141,200** | **Schedule C Line 1** |
| Business bank deposits, per bookkeeper | 147,379 | Starting point — cash deposits method check only |
| Less: transfer from personal savings | (6,000) | Not accession to wealth, not §61 income |
| Less: DesignKit Pro refund credited to bank | (1,400) | Not gross receipts; same-year reduction of expense |
| Adjusted deposits, net-of-fee basis | 139,979 |  |
| Add back: PayFlow fee withheld: $40,700 x 3% | 1,221 | 1099-K is gross; fee is separate deduction, §162 |
| **Gross receipts, per bank as adjusted** | **141,200** |  |
| **Unexplained difference** | **0** | Returns and bank tie. Keep this schedule — IRS matching will show $159,200 of 1099s vs. $141,200 reported. |

Proof: $62,000 + ($56,500-$18,000) + $39,479 PayFlow net + $6,000 + $1,400 = $147,379.

## 2. Schedule C — Profit or Loss

| Sch C Line | Item | Amount ($) | Rule applied |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gross receipts | 141,200 | §61; cash received. See §1 above. |
| 10 | Commissions — PayFlow 3% merchant fee | 1,221 | §162 ordinary/necessary; deductible because income reported gross. $40,700 x 3%. |
| 11 | Contract labor — John Stiles | 9,000 | §162; deductible if business purpose paid. 1099 compliance still required — see §4. |
| 18 | Office expense — software subscriptions, net | 3,460 | §162; $4,860 paid less $1,400 same-year refund. Refund reduces expense, not income. |
| 24a | Travel — airfare + hotel, client conference | 2,130 | §162; away-from-home overnight for business. |
| 24b | Deductible meals | 1,600 | §162 + §274(n)(1), (d): 50% of $3,200 restaurant meals, logged attendees/business purpose. |
| 27a Other | Laptop — de minimis safe harbor | 2,400 | Reg. §1.263(a)-1(f); <$2,500/invoice without AFS if election attached and expensed on books. 100% business use. |
| 44 | Car/truck — standard mileage | 2,814 | Notice 2024-8: 4,200 mi x $0.67. No actual-cost records, so standard rate required. §274(d) log required. |
| 30 | Home office, simplified | 1,200 | Rev. Proc. 2013-13: 240 sq ft exclusive use x $5, <300 max. |
| — | **Total expenses** | **23,825** |  |
| 31 | **Net profit** | **117,375** |  |

**Excluded from Schedule C:**

* Health insurance $7,800 — Not Schedule C. §162(l) adjustment on **Schedule 1 Line 17**, limited to net SE profit. Limit not binding here.
* Gym $720 — Nondeductible personal expense, §262. Subjective business benefit insufficient under §162.
* $6,000 savings transfer, $1,400 refund — excluded per §1.

## 3. Self-Employment Tax

Net earnings subject to SE tax: $117,375 x 92.35% = **$108,396**

Assumes no other wages/SE income; full $108,396 < $168,600 2024 Social Security wage base.

| Component | Computation | Amount ($) |
|---|---|---|
| Social Security 12.4% | $108,396 x 12.4% | 13,441 |
| Medicare 2.9% | $108,396 x 2.9% | 3,144 |
| **SE tax — Schedule SE** | **15.3% x $108,396** | **16,585** |
| **Deductible one-half — Schedule 1** | $16,585 x 50% | **8,292** |

No 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax — below $200,000 single threshold.
Self-employed health insurance $7,800 fully allowable as Schedule 1 adjustment: net profit $117,375 > premium, Jane not eligible for employer plan.

Resulting adjustments to income: $8,292 + $7,800 = $16,092, before AGI/QBI considerations.

## 4. Open Items, Risks, Recommendations

**Research note NOT relied on:** No. 3 — 2022 blog claiming 100% restaurant meals. That was temporary relief for 2021-2022 only under §210, Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021. For 2024, §274(n)(1) restores 50%. All other notes relied on.

**Recommendation — laptop $2,400: elect de minimis safe harbor and expense currently.**
Under $2,500 threshold, one invoice, no AFS. Gives 100% 2024 deduction with no Form 4562, no 5-year MACRS, no 60% bonus limitation for 2024, and no §179/§280F recapture risk. Must attach §1.263(a)-1(f) election to timely return and ensure books treat it as expense. Alternative — capitalize + §179 or 60% bonus + MACRS — defers part of deduction and adds complexity for no benefit.

**Compliance still needed:**

1. **1099-NEC to Stiles:** Obtain Form W-9 now; file/ furnish 2024 Form 1099-NEC ($9,000) by Jan. 31, 2025. Penalties §§6721/6722, plus backup-withholding risk. Confirm employee vs. contractor classification.
2. **Mileage log:** Obtain contemporaneous log for 4,200 miles — date, business purpose, destination. Without §274(d) substantiation, $2,814 disallowed on exam.
3. **Home office:** Confirm 240 sq ft exclusive + regular use and that records support principal place of business. Retain diagram/photo.
4. **Software refund:** Confirm $4,860 and $1,400 both in 2024. If expense was 2023, refund is 2024 Other Income, and 2024 deduction is $4,860.
5. **Documentation to retain:** PayFlow monthly statements proving $1,221 fee, Bluefin statement proving $18,000 overlap, bank proof transfer was personal, health-eligibility certification by month.
6. **Estimates/QBI:** Consider 2025 estimates to avoid §6654 penalty; model §199A QBI deduction — not computed here for lack of taxable-income data.
